label: Safe D

model.rationale: The seat's D+22 lean and the Democratic nominee's clear financial and outside-spending advantage make a Republican upset implausible; markets agree at 98%. The margin is set slightly below the fundamentals-based figure to reflect the open seat and absence of polling.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending on the Republican side could narrow the expected margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Detroit-area MI-13 is a heavily Democratic district with a partisan lean of D+22. Shri Thanedar lost his renomination bid, so this is an open seat, but the Democratic nominee Donavan McKinney enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised about $1.4 million and benefited from roughly $850,000 in outside support. Republican nominee T.P. Nykoriak reports no fundraising or outside spending on file.

With no general-election polls available, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic hold. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at 98 percent. Minor-party and independent candidates are on the ballot but lack visible resources. The seat remains safely in Democratic hands, with the main uncertainty being the exact size of the margin rather than the winner.
